purpose: Interpretive calls I made during portal-PDF → JSON extraction. Tamara should sanity-check each one and either confirm or fix in the source JSON before downstream sync to BuilderTrend.

conventions.compound_rows_split: Portal rows naming multiple surfaces (e.g. 'Backsplash / Tub & Vanity / Inside Niche') were split into one entry per physical surface with the same tile spec.
conventions.brand_separator: Portal 'Brand X / Y' parsed as brand=X, style=Y when Y looked like a collection name.
conventions.size_field: Portal 'Size' has no schema column — values were appended to notes (e.g. '12x24').
conventions.size_in_notes: Tile size lives in notes since the schema doesn't have a size column. Add a size column in a future migration if querying by size becomes important.
conventions.unknown_brand_marker: Entries where the portal listed only a color number with no brand are marked brand='Unknown' with the notes field flagging the ambiguity.

interpretive_calls.portal_text: Backsplash / Tub & Vanity / Inside Niche — Brand: Dal, Color: Remedy RD 20
interpretive_calls.decision: Split into 3 entries: vanity_backsplash, tub_surround, shower_niche. Treated 'Backsplash' and 'Vanity' as the same physical surface (vanity backsplash).
interpretive_calls.needs_review: Confirm 'Backsplash' meant vanity backsplash and not a separate wall.

interpretive_calls.decision: Set brand='Unknown', moved 'Lana ZL 07' into style, flagged in notes.

interpretive_calls.portal_text: Bedrosians Magnifico Calcutto Oro — Matte on floor, Polished on walls
interpretive_calls.decision: Two entries: floor (color='Calcutto Oro Matte') and shower_walls (color='Calcutto Oro Polished').
interpretive_calls.needs_review: Should these be the same SKU with finish as a notes detail, or treated as 2 SKUs since matte and polished are different products?

interpretive_calls.portal_text: Wall Tub / Splashes / Inside Niche — Dal Contempoee Jasmine CE30, 4x4 ring pattern
interpretive_calls.decision: Three entries: tub_surround + vanity_backsplash + shower_niche.
interpretive_calls.needs_review: Standard split; confirm 'Wall Tub' is tub_surround vs a separate accent wall.

interpretive_calls.issue: Brand variants for the same vendor
interpretive_calls.portal_text: Brands like 'Dal', 'Dal Spirit', 'Dal/Miramo', 'Dal/Remedy', 'Dal/Marble Attache' appear — sometimes 'Dal' is just the vendor, sometimes 'Dal Spirit' is a sub-brand.
interpretive_calls.decision: Kept the literal first-token as brand. 'Dal Spirit' was preserved as a separate brand. 'Dal/Miramo' parsed as brand=Dal, style=Miramo.
interpretive_calls.needs_review: Consider a brand-normalization pass that maps 'Dal Spirit' → 'Dal' so the autocomplete groups all Daltile entries together.

interpretive_calls.issue: Masonry Center vs Bedrosians distributor ambiguity
interpretive_calls.portal_text: Masonry Center carries multiple manufacturers (Marazzi, Portabello, Lungarno, Ragno). Portal lists 'Masonry Center / Marazzi' style entries.
interpretive_calls.decision: Kept brand='Masonry Center' (the distributor) with the manufacturer as style. This is consistent across all extractions.
interpretive_calls.needs_review: If Tamara wants to fuzzy-match by manufacturer (Marazzi) rather than distributor (Masonry Center), the brand-vs-style split should flip.

recommended_review_order: 1. Skim 'interpretive_calls' for the 3 'Brand missing → Unknown' cases — fill in actual brand if you can.
2. Walk through a few projects in /selections/:id and visually check that the location vocabulary matches reality.
3. The general 'Dal Spirit' / 'Masonry Center' normalization questions are policy decisions — answer once, apply globally with a sed pass on seed/bath-tile/.
4. The compound-row splits are the highest-leverage check: if your tile sub gets ordering quantities wrong because of how I split, fixing those JSONs first prevents the same issue on future imports.
